issues.legal_issue: Land used for grazing cattle or cutting grass as a bid land falls within the agricultural land covered by the agricultural ceiling law.
material_facts: The disputed lands were identified as bid lands and were used or intended for grazing cattle or cutting grass for cattle.
The earlier regional enactments described bid land by reference to grazing and cutting grass, while the agricultural ceiling law included raising grass and using land for grazing within agriculture.
The landholder’s agricultural operations could be carried out under the supervision of family members or through hired labour.
issues.conclusion: The bid lands fell within the definitions of agriculture and land in the unamended agricultural ceiling law and were subject to its ceiling restrictions.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(1), 2(3), 2(11), 2(12), 2(17), and 6 of the Gujarat Agricultural Lands Ceiling Act, 1960, read together, cover land used or capable of being used for agriculture, including raising grass and grazing. The descriptions of bid land in Sections 2(6) and 2(18) of the Saurashtra Land Reforms Act, 1951, Section 2(ii) of the Saurashtra Barkhali Abolition Act, 1951, and Section 2(a) of the Saurashtra Estates Acquisition Act, 1952, help identify its character. Nagbhai Najbhai Khackar v. State of Gujarat supports treating bid land used for grazing as agricultural land; its additional reason on that point was also binding. London Jewellers Ltd. v. Attenborough, Jacobs v. London County Council, Behrens v. Bertram Mills Circus Ltd., and Smt. Somawanti v. State of Punjab support treating each ground supporting a prior decision as binding.

predicates.agricultural_ceiling_proceeding: A proceeding was brought to determine whether land holdings exceeded an agricultural ceiling.
predicates.bid_land_identified: The land was identified as land reserved or held for grazing cattle or cutting grass for cattle.
predicates.land_used_for_grazing_or_grass: The land was used, or was held for use, for grazing cattle or raising or cutting grass.

issues.definition: When a proceeding determines whether holdings exceed an agricultural ceiling, land identified as bid land and used for grazing or grass counts as agricultural land for that ceiling.

issues.legal_issue: The urban land ceiling law does not displace the agricultural ceiling law as to agricultural land merely because that land lies within an urban agglomeration.
material_facts: The disputed lands lay within an urban agglomeration covered by the urban land ceiling law.
The urban land ceiling law excluded land mainly used for agriculture from its relevant definitions of urban or vacant land.
The lands were bid lands that fell within the agricultural land definitions of the unamended agricultural ceiling law.
issues.conclusion: The urban land ceiling law did not prevent the agricultural ceiling law, in its unamended form, from applying to the agricultural lands.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(o), 2(q), and 6 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, together with the explanations to Section 2(o), exclude qualifying agricultural land from the urban ceiling regime. Article 252(1) and (2) of the Constitution govern legislation enacted following a State resolution. Thumati Venkaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh explains that an agricultural ceiling law may operate on land before the urban ceiling law applies to land within its field; Union of India v. Valluri Basavaiah Chowdhary addresses the scope of Parliament’s authority under Article 252. The Court held that the unamended agricultural ceiling law continued to operate on agricultural land outside the urban law’s effective reach.

rule.if: challenge_to_agricultural_ceiling_action and land_is_agricultural and land_within_urban_agglomeration and urban_ceiling_law_excludes_agricultural_land

predicates.challenge_to_agricultural_ceiling_action: A party challenged action taken to determine or acquire land exceeding an agricultural ceiling.
predicates.land_is_agricultural: The land was used or capable of being used for agriculture, including grazing or raising grass.
predicates.land_within_urban_agglomeration: The land lay within an area treated as an urban agglomeration.
predicates.urban_ceiling_law_excludes_agricultural_: The urban land ceiling regime excluded land mainly used for agriculture from its coverage.

issues.definition: If a challenge concerns an agricultural ceiling action on agricultural land within an urban agglomeration, and the urban regime excludes agricultural land, the urban regime does not displace the agricultural ceiling law.

issues.legal_issue: A prior decision concerning different land and distinct factual circumstances does not bar a later land-ceiling dispute under res judicata.
material_facts: The earlier proceedings relied on concerned bid lands in a different area and involved different parties and land.
Those lands had been classified for residential use in a master plan, while the disputed lands were considered bid lands and the earlier proceedings did not concern them.
The respondent relied on government affidavits and a decision concerning those other lands to argue that the State was barred from applying the agricultural ceiling law.
issues.conclusion: Res judicata did not apply because the parties, land, and material factual circumstances were different.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires, among other things, that the matter directly and substantially in issue have been between the same parties, or parties claiming under them, and have been heard and finally decided. The Court distinguished Palitana Sugar Mills (P) Ltd. v. State of Gujarat because the prior determination concerned different lands and a distinct classification.

rule.if: challenge_to_land_ceiling_order and prior_decision_concerned_different_land and prior_decision_involved_different_parties and prior_decision_rest_on_distinct_material_facts

predicates.challenge_to_land_ceiling_order: A party challenged an order determining land in excess of a ceiling.
predicates.prior_decision_concerned_different_land: The earlier proceeding concerned land other than the land in the later dispute.
predicates.prior_decision_involved_different_partie: The earlier proceeding did not involve the same parties or persons claiming under them.
predicates.prior_decision_rest_on_distinct_material: The earlier decision depended on factual circumstances, such as a different land classification, that were not present in the later dispute.

issues.definition: A prior decision about different land, involving different parties and distinct material facts, does not bar a later challenge to a land-ceiling order.

issues.legal_issue: Removal of a constitutional bar that had made an otherwise valid law unenforceable allows that law to operate without reenactment.
material_facts: The agricultural ceiling law had been enacted within the State’s legislative field.
The urban land ceiling law had been enacted following a State resolution, and the parties disputed the effect of that law on the continued operation of the agricultural ceiling law.
The urban land ceiling law was later repealed, removing the asserted constitutional impediment.
issues.conclusion: Upon repeal of the urban land ceiling law, the constitutional impediment ceased and the agricultural ceiling law could operate without fresh enactment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle in M.P.V. Sundararamier & Co. v. State of Andhra Pradesh: where a law is within the legislature’s domain but is unenforceable because of a constitutional prohibition, removal of that prohibition permits the law to operate without reenactment; this differs from a law that was outside legislative competence and void from inception.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and earlier_law_within_legislative_domain and earlier_law_unenforceable_only_due_to_constitutional_bar and constitutional_bar_later_removed

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: A proceeding concerned the operation of a law regulating land holdings or land ceilings.
predicates.earlier_law_within_legislative_domain: The earlier law was enacted on a subject within the enacting legislature’s competence.
predicates.earlier_law_unenforceable_only_due_to_co: The earlier law was otherwise valid but could not be enforced because of a constitutional prohibition.
predicates.constitutional_bar_later_removed: A later event removed the constitutional prohibition that had prevented enforcement.

issues.definition: When a land-ceiling proceeding concerns an otherwise valid law that was unenforceable only because of a constitutional bar, removing that bar permits the law to operate without reenactment.
